newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends slightly up in quiet deals.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends slightly up in quiet deals.

text.p: The Philippine peso ended sligthly up at 26.373 on Tuesday from 26.374 as the Central Bank's 20 percent overnight borrowing rate kept speculators away, traders said.
The day's average was unchanged at 26.373, with volume light at $131 million.
"The peso just moved sideways. There was no Central Bank intervention in buying or selling dollars," a trader said.
The peso, however, hit an intraday low of 26.374 as some banks continued to be wary in case the U.S. raised interest rates and domestic rates eased, traders said.
The U.S. Federal Open Market committee is meeting on Tuesday to decide on interest rates.
Banks are also watching out for the lowering of the Central Bank's overnight borrowing rate after it was raised several times last week to fight speculation caused by the problems of the Thai baht.
